misconceptions.reachability: Each misconception ID is reached by wrong options or registered wrong values in at least 2 different items

report.answerTypes: P8 and B9 probabilities use R (exact fractions); interval answers use I; root/extremum position answers use S; counts and values use N

C11: Worked example f=x^3-3x+1: f'=3(x+1)(x-1); local max f(-1)=3, local min f(1)=-1
Prediction f'=(x+1)(x-2)^2 = x^3-3x^2+4; its own derivative 3x(x-2) puts the peak of f' at x=0 (f'(0)=4). f increases for x>=-1; only extremum is a min at -1; none at 2
basic x^3-3x^2-9x+2: local max 7, decreasing on [-1,3] (wrong: -25, -1, open interval)
transfer f'=(x-1)^2(x-4): f' is <=0 for x<4 and rises on (3,4) while still negative, so f decreases on (-inf,4]; only extremum is a min at x=4
error analysis x^4-4x^3: f'=4x^2(x-3); only extremum is x=3 with value -27; flawed step is ③
entry x^3-27x: f'<0 has 5 integer solutions (wrong: 7)
P8: Dice, sum 8: 5 outcomes, 2 contain a 3, so 2/5. Reverse condition: at least one 3 has 36-25=11 outcomes, 2 of them sum to 8, so 2/11. Other wrongs: 1/18, 1/3 (counting unordered pairs)
Non-replacement, R3 W2: second red has 6+6=12 of 20 outcomes, both red 6, so 1/2 (wrong: 3/10, 3/5)
entry: 5 outcomes for sum 8; multiples of 6 up to 20 give 3/20 (wrong: 3/10)
Coin counterexample: given at least one head, P(two heads)=1/3, not 1/2
